blocks.text: Analysis of the above equation reveals that there are four unknown quantities, v⃗₁f, v⃗₂f, θ₁, θ₂. If these quantities can be measured, conservation of momentum and energy can be proved using equation (2.34), (2.35) and (2.36).

blocks.title: Interesting Information
blocks.text: Some of the kinetic energy is transferred into other forms such as heat, sound, and deformation in inelastic collision. For example, the collision is inelastic if a bullet is fired into a block of wood. This is because some energy of the bullet is lost in the form of sound and heat. Similarly, if a ball is dropped on a floor from a certain height, it does not rebound to the same height because its kinetic energy is lost in other forms of energies, like sound energy and heat energy.

blocks.title: Example 2.9
blocks.problem: A particle 'A' of mass 1 kg is moving with initial velocity 5 m s⁻¹ towards right collides with stationary target 'B' of same mass at rest. After collision the particle 'A' moves at an angle of 30° above horizontal with a speed of 3 m s⁻¹ and particle 'B' moves with the horizontal at an angle of 53° with a speed of 4 m s⁻¹. Prove that collision is elastic in nature.
steps:
Initial momentum = m₁v₁i + m₂v₂i
= (1 kg × 5 m s⁻¹) + (1 kg × 0 m s⁻¹) = 5 kg m s⁻¹

Final momentum in x-direction = m₁v₁f + m₂v₂f
= (1 kg × 3 m s⁻¹ × cos30°) + (1 kg × 4 m s⁻¹ × cos53°)
= 2.60 kg m s⁻¹ + 2.40 kg m s⁻¹
= 5 kg m s⁻¹

As momentum is conserved in x-direction, therefore,
(K.E)i = ½m₁v₁i² + ½m₂v₂i²
= (½ × 1 × (5)²) + (½ × 1 × 0) = 12.5 J
blocks.answer: As both momentum and K.E. are conserved, indicating that collision is elastic.
